_comment: Single source of truth for harness guardrails. Deny-only: Codex 0.148 cannot rewrite a command (updatedInput is unreachable), so every rule blocks and explains instead of correcting. Matching is argv-head based, never substring, so the banned word appearing inside a document body does not trip a rule. Rules are only as strong as the matcher in guard.py; see its docstring. Paths and host names here are the ones for the example estate in the README; edit them to match yours.

rules.message: BLOCKED (teleport-only): direct SSH is banned on this estate. Use `tsh ssh ops-agent@<node>` to run a command, or `tsh scp` to copy a file. Nodes: hv-1, hv-2, workstation-a, workstation-b, console, and the *-win variants. If `tsh` reports an expired certificate, stop and tell the operator to run `tsh login`. There is no workaround.
BLOCKED (destructive-storage): commands that write a partition table or a raw block device belong to the operator, not to an agent. Report what you believe needs doing and let the operator run it.
BLOCKED (destructive-storage): `dd` writing to a block device belongs to the operator. Reading from a device (`if=/dev/...`) is fine; writing is not.
BLOCKED (destructive-storage): naming a raw block device as a write target belongs to the operator. This covers redirects and `tee` as well as `dd`. Reading a device is fine.
BLOCKED (destructive-storage): `btrfs device delete` belongs to the operator.
BLOCKED (destructive-storage): deleting an EFI boot entry belongs to the operator. `efibootmgr` without -B (listing) is allowed.
BLOCKED (media-drives): nothing under /mnt/media* is ever deleted or overwritten. This is an absolute rule. Transcodes and conversions read from there and write NEW files to a different destination.
BLOCKED (media-drives): `find ... -delete` / `-exec` under /mnt/media* is a deletion path. Listing is allowed; acting on the results is not.

rules._paths_note: An entry ending in / protects the directory as a whole (the dir itself or dir/*); an entry without protects every path under that prefix.
rules.message: BLOCKED (secrets): secret material is never read into a transcript. Use the credential broker (`sudo -n -u broker secret-broker-run ...`), which passes the secret to the child process without exposing it, or SOPS for encrypted files. Never print, copy, or commit a secret value.
BLOCKED (rm-root): recursive force-delete of a filesystem root, a top-level directory, or a glob directly beneath one. If you meant a specific subdirectory, name it explicitly.

BLOCKED (proxmox-mutate): changing container or VM state needs explicit operator confirmation, whether it runs locally or inside a `tsh ssh` remote command. This rule exists because a subagent briefed for read-only reconnaissance ran `sudo pct start 907 2>/dev/null; true` and started a container whose static IP collided with a running one. Read-only inspection is still available: `pct config`, `pct list`, `pct status`, `qm config`, `qm list`, `qm status`. To change state, say what you want changed and why, and let the operator confirm it.

BLOCKED (forced-success-probe): this command discards stderr and then forces a success status, so a failure, or a state change you did not intend, leaves no trace in the transcript. That combination is what hid the container-907 incident. Suppressing stderr on its own is fine, and so is `|| true` on its own; using both together is not. Run the command plainly and read the error.

messages.indirect-dispatch: BLOCKED (indirect-dispatch): the command name comes from a shell variable or an unexpanded substitution, so the guard cannot see what would actually run. Write the command out literally.
